commits.message:
Copy the build lock into the interactive-emulator test's scratch tree

The interactive-emulator setup now imports build-lock.js, so the isolated
producer tree the test builds needs it beside the setup module.

Claim the script-source lookup rows and mark the deleted derived files historical

The script-source lookup work added a generated Aiken module written by a
midgard-validation suite but no channel for it, so the channel table check
refused the tree; it now has one. Two docs cite files P1 deleted, and two skill
rules lost their enforcement tags in the merge.

Merge the script-source lookup work into the P1 derived-values branch

Upstream re-took three fit ledgers and both blueprint fixtures for the
script-source change; those files are deleted here, so the merge keeps the
deletions. The new step-04 reference capture drops the ledger kind argument
like its neighbours, and the trace-preparation cap takes upstream's value
without the size-change note.

Drop the two module-size caps the fit-ledger deletion made obsolete

Deleting the fit-ledger writers took both lifecycle tests under 500 lines,
and a cap for a file within the limit is refused.

Merge branch 'colll78/p1-fixtures' into colll78/p1-derived-values

With the DA and watcher fixtures derived per run, no channel reads the
blueprint any more, so the @blueprint input sets go and the skill says no
channel check needs a fresh build. The blueprint-freshness blind spot is closed
by the suites' stamp setup, which now rebuilds a stale blueprint.

Rebuild a missing or stale blueprint in the test suites' stamp setup

The stamp setup refused a run whose default blueprint was stale and let a
run without one start and fail file by file. It now makes the blueprint
fresh before any file starts, the way contrib prepares one: copied from a
checkout with identical inputs, else built with deployment:build. One run
builds under a lock in onchain/aiken/build/ while parallel runs wait for it.
The run is refused only when the pinned compiler is unavailable or the stamp
cannot be judged; a blueprint named by MIDGARD_REAL_BLUEPRINT_PATH is still
refused unless its build record is fresh.

The MIDGARD_BLUEPRINT_STAMP=warn downgrade is gone, with the guards in
contrib and the SDK suite evidence that refused it. The interactive-emulator
blueprint build shares the new lock module.

Merge branch 'colll78/p1-fit' into colll78/p1-derived-values

Both lanes deleted their ledger kind from the channel table and the skill, so
the merge keeps neither: execution costs are ceilings and Van Rossem fit is
checked at submission. The discovery patterns for both file shapes stay, so a
recreated ledger is flagged as unclaimed. Also documents the two channels
(cek-cost-v1-aiken, cek-program-large-integer) the skill's own test reported
missing from channels.md.

Delete the Van Rossem fit ledgers now that every submission is checked

The emulator submit guard judges every transaction of every run against
the Van Rossem byte, memory and CPU limits on the current build. The
saved fit ledgers, their afterAll writers and collectors, the pinned and
split ledger checks, the regenerate command and its CI step only restated
that check from a past run, and could drift from the build they claimed
to describe.

Remove all of them along with MIDGARD_WRITE_FIT_LEDGER and fit:regenerate,
keep each test's per-submission assertions, and point the skills, size
plan docs and audit notes at the guard instead. The availability
challenge fit summary stays because its design note cites it.

Judge script execution costs against one ceiling table

The ten execution ledgers pinned exact readings, so every on-chain change that
moved a cost, even downward, had to re-take a ledger before CI went green. They
become one table, demo/midgard-core/src/script-budgets.json, read by CI and by
production alike. Each entry is a ceiling: a reading above it fails, a reading
that shrinks needs no edit. Rows production reads keep a ceiling equal to the
current reading, so planner and estimator output is unchanged; the rest get 1%
headroom, capped at the basis. onchain/aiken/scripts/script-budgets.mjs checks
the table, tightens it to fresh readings, or raises one ceiling with a reason.

Entries above the basis still fail if the reading comes to fit, and growth
claims keep their band. Interpolated and extrapolated rows that were never
measured are dropped rather than carried as ceilings.

Derive the DA deployment input and watcher initialization frame per run

Both fixtures were blueprint outputs committed as JSON: every validator change
made them stale, and a test existed only to say so and to regenerate them
behind a MIDGARD_WRITE_* flag. They are now produced from the run's own
blueprint, once per run, by the code that generated them.

deriveDaDeploymentInfo applies the real contracts with synthetic reference
outpoints, as the generation test did. deriveWatcherInitializationFrame runs
the real node atomic initialization on an emulator with fixed wallets,
protocol parameters and a fixed wall clock, so the frame is the same bytes on
every run of one blueprint. The clock is held through a faked Date for the
production only, because the node's reference-script publication compares
the auth policy's deadline with Date.now(); the initialization tests keep the
real clock.

The DA committee and watcher suites read the derived values and keep their
behavioural assertions. The DA suite now builds on the blueprint stamp and
loads raw SQL, since the producer reaches midgard-node's sources; the watcher
derives only in its testing-profile project, which reads the same blueprint
as the producer.

Removed with them: the committed-equals-regenerated test, the watcher write
branch and its blueprint-hash pin in the initialization test, both channels
and the skill steps that regenerated them.

Move the run-shared fixture directory into midgard-test-support

Values derived from the blueprint are about to be shared by the DA committee
and watcher suites as well as the node's, so the run-scoped directory, its
claim lock and its global setup move out of midgard-node's tests into
midgard-test-support, unchanged in behaviour. memoizeForRun adds the shape
those suites need: produce a value once per run, publish it atomically for
every other worker, and hand each caller its own copy. The directory is new
each run, so there is no cache key to keep correct.

The workspace bundle analysis now also walks the absolute global setups a
package exports, so a setup that imports a module tests import too is served
from the same bundle instead of being refused as a second instance.

Judge every emulator submission against the Van Rossem limits

The publication target (15,872 bytes for a transaction with zero execution
units) was enforced only while a test built its fit ledger, so a test that
measured no ledger row could submit an oversized publication unnoticed.
The limits now live in proof-fit/van-rossem.ts as constants plus
assertFitsVanRossem, and a vitest setup file layers it over
Emulator.prototype.submitTx for every project in the suite, so each signed
transaction any emulator is asked to accept is judged before the emulator
sees it. The emulator itself checks neither transaction size nor execution
units. The traced-refusal run stays exempt, as its publication envelope
already is.

Show on-chain ABI and size movement in the PR summary

A pull request touching the validators now gets a job summary listing the
validators and reached definitions whose interface changed, and the largest
compiled-size movements, read off fresh blueprints built at the merge base and
at the head. It replaces reading committed derived files as the way a reviewer
sees on-chain impact: nothing is committed, so no change has to re-sync a
snapshot to keep CI green. The job is informational and not a merge gate.

Hold module-size caps as ceilings

Each module-size exception required its file to be exactly the recorded
length, so a file that got shorter failed until someone edited its entry.
Across the branch history that rule produced hundreds of commits whose only
change was a lowered max, and it never resisted growth better than a ceiling
would: ESLint max-lines already enforces the ceiling for demo TS/JS.

A cap now fails only when the file grows past it, or when the file is back
within the 500-line limit and the exception is obsolete. Shrinking needs no
edit. The size-change notes appended to 118 reasons are removed, and the
validator refuses new ones: a reason says why a file stays large, and its size
history lives in git.
